subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw add YAML/YML as a supported core config file format, or keep JSON5 `openclaw.json` plus CLI/RPC config mutation as the only core config-file contract?
rationale: The current source and docs define one JSON5 config-file contract, and adding YAML would expand a compatibility-sensitive core config surface rather than repair a broken existing behavior.

options.title: Keep JSON5 canonical
options.body: Confirm JSON5 `openclaw.json` plus `openclaw config` and `config.patch` as the supported path, with docs clarifying comment-safe programmatic edits if needed.

options.title: Approve YAML config
options.body: Require a design and PR covering `.yaml`/`.yml` precedence, parser semantics, write-back behavior, hot reload, doctor, docs, security, and upgrade tests.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 canonical
recommendation.body: Confirm JSON5 `openclaw.json` plus `openclaw config` and `config.patch` as the supported path, with docs clarifying comment-safe programmatic edits if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing candidate from recent current-line blame and docs/config-policy history for deciding whether the documented config contract should expand.
